headline: Medium risk: Copilot can write repo files while Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content, creating plausible prompt-injection and data-flow hazards; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can write repo files and read repo context, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and knowledge-base content. No direct shared channel is documented, so the main pathway is manual or indirect content transfer rather than automatic hijack. That makes prompt injection plausible but limited.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text is copied into Notion pages as instructions, Notion AI may follow it.
IF a shared document is used as a bridge between repo notes and workspace pages, malicious text can propagate.
mitigations: Keep Copilot output out of Notion instruction pages.
Add a short provenance note before pasted AI text.
Review any AI-authored page before asking Notion AI to summarize it.
Use separate pages for raw AI output and human-approved guidance.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and Notion AI can access workspace pages and databases under the user's permissions. Even without a documented direct bridge, copying code or notes between them can expose sensitive material to Notion's vendor-hosted backend and downstream model providers.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are pasted into Notion pages, Notion AI can process them.
IF Copilot-generated repo context is moved into workspace pages, sensitive content may leave the code environment.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets or proprietary code into Notion pages.
Restrict Notion pages used with AI to non-sensitive summaries.
Use redaction before moving content from editor buffers to workspace pages.
Mark sensitive pages as off-limits for AI-assisted Q&A.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can modify git state and write the filesystem, while Notion AI cannot write files or modify git state. The profiles show overlapping read-like content domains only through user-mediated transfer, so direct write-write conflict is absent and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF a human copies Notion output into a repo and then Copilot edits the same files, merge confusion can occur.
IF the workspace is used as a staging area for code changes, conflicting edits may be introduced manually.
mitigations: Keep Notion notes separate from active repo branches.
Use one source of truth for code changes.
Review diffs before applying Copilot suggestions.
Avoid round-tripping the same content between Notion and the repo.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is RAG-style over workspace content, and Copilot Workspace plans and applies edits for human review. If Copilot-produced facts or code summaries are copied into Notion and then treated as authoritative, errors can cascade across both systems despite the human-review step.
conditions: IF Copilot output is pasted into Notion without verification, Notion AI may summarize or amplify the error.
IF Notion summaries are then used to guide Copilot edits, the same mistake can propagate into code changes.
mitigations: Verify Copilot outputs before pasting them into Notion.
Treat Notion summaries as drafts, not source of truth.
Cross-check any code facts against the repository before editing.
Require a human to confirm claims before applying changes.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot handles source code and open editor buffers, while Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge-base content under workspace permissions. If regulated or sensitive data is moved between these vendor-hosted systems, retention and residency obligations can diverge; the profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages and then queried by AI, compliance review is required.
IF code repositories contain customer or employee data and are summarized into workspace pages, retention policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AI-queried pages.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive content.
Add a manual review step before sharing code-derived notes.
Check vendor retention settings for both tools.
